title: Greenpanel Industries Ltd - 542857 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Greenpanel Q1 FY27 combined revenue rose 8.5% to INR350 crore and EBITDA turned positive at INR32.5 crore, but exports fell to zero and OEM volumes degrew 14%.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue grew 8.5% YoY to INR350 crore on a combined basis, with MDF operating EBITDA margin at 10.3% versus 4.4% a year earlier. Price hikes of around 15% taken in April were largely rolled back by peers through May to July, so realisations are now close to pre-hike levels. Exports fell to zero and OEM sales degrew 14%, while domestic MDF volumes grew 12% YoY and retail MDF grew about 20%. Management declined to give margin or utilisation guidance, citing daily chemical cost and discount volatility.

financial_highlights.metric: Consolidated operating EBITDA (ex-euro ECB currency impact)

financial_highlights.change: vs loss of INR12.4 crore in Q1 FY26
from INR353 crore at start of quarter

financial_highlights.value: INR2.5 crore overall, INR1.8 crore on ECB

segments.name: MDF (retail)
segments.commentary: Retail MDF grew about 20% YoY and domestic MDF volumes grew 12% YoY, the fourth consecutive quarter of domestic volume growth. Retail is about 75-80% of the mix.

segments.name: MDF (OEM)
segments.commentary: OEM sales degrew 14% YoY after management chose not to supply at discounted prices during the chemical shortage; OEM is about 20-25% of mix.

segments.name: MDF (exports)
segments.commentary: Exports fell to zero in Q1 as freight rose from about $400-500 to $5,500-6,000 per container; Middle East made up about 80-85% of past exports and remains effectively shut, with July and August exports negligible.

segments.name: Plywood
segments.commentary: Volumes +10.4% YoY and revenue +5% YoY; around 5% price hike taken in Q1, with only a small part passed on as schemes. Management said QoQ plywood margin fell from 7.5% to 2.7% on product mix and higher fixed costs.

guidance_outlook: No quantitative margin or capacity utilisation guidance given; management cited chemical cost and discount volatility.
Management aims to ramp domestic volumes over the remaining nine months to improve full-year market share versus peers.
Management said the objective is to maintain Q1 margins, with possible lag in passing on any future price hikes.
Management expects pricing and demand pressure to persist through FY27, with improvement hoped for in FY28.
Management said double-digit MDF margins are not a very tough ask if volumes and utilisation rise; current utilisation is about 50-60%.
No MDF growth capex needed for 18-24 months beyond maintenance; plywood capacity to rise 30-40% via minimal debottlenecking investment.
capex_capacity: MDF utilisation is around 50-60% (cited as about 51% in Q&A); management intends to enhance utilisation this year, subject to market volumes and exports.
Action has a new line coming in South India and another continuous press is coming up in Madhya Pradesh.
Plywood: plan to fully utilise current capacity, then add machinery in existing facility at minimal investment to lift output 30-40%.
Maintenance shutdown: 5-7 day line shutdown taken this quarter due to lack of orders; management prefers splitting maintenance into short shutdowns rather than a 15-day stop.
Working capital up 4 days QoQ on higher finished goods and timber inventory for seasonality, but still 5 days leaner YoY.
demand_pricing: Peers rolled back the approximately 15% April price hike in phases through May, June and July; management said almost all of the hike is now rolled back, with 1-2% retained in some segments and markets.
Management said the company now prices OEMs at par with peers rather than at a premium to Century, to regain OEM volumes.
Channel partners are holding inventory on a hand-to-mouth basis, with destocking in Q1 and expected to persist given volatile prices.

Management estimates industry growth at mid-teens in the prior quarter; Arun Baid noted Greenpanel had the lowest industry growth in India this quarter and Century has out-volumed Greenpanel for two quarters.
Chemical costs are about 4-5% above pre-war levels and rising again; timber costs are stable, and mixed wood is being used in place of eucalyptus.
Q1 cost savings from timber and efficiencies were about 6-7% combined, and low-cost inventory from last fiscal helped gross margin.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company diversify export markets given the drop in exports?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is exploring other markets, but freight volatility and foreign manufacturing make it hard to compete; alternative markets cannot replace lost Middle East volumes.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 7.4% ASP increase due to channel mix shift to retail?
qa_highlights.answer: Partly. A large part came from removing OEM discounts, so OEM sales came through at near retail prices, shifting mix toward retail price levels.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the company not the price maker as market leader?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it avoids undercutting and does not lead on rollbacks, but takes the lead on hikes; averaging out export pricing into the domestic market would have triggered further price cuts.

qa_highlights.question: Why has market share been lost and what is the game plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 OEM sales were intentionally held back during chemical shortage; the company now plans to price at par with peers and focus on volume and utilisation, with the aim of regaining share from Q2 FY27 on a smaller base.

qa_highlights.question: Can margins be sustained if raw material costs fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to maintain Q1 margins; if chemical costs rise again, the industry may take another price hike, with some lag.

qa_highlights.question: Is growth capex planned over the next 18-24 months?
qa_highlights.answer: No MDF capex beyond maintenance; a small plywood debottlenecking investment to add 30-40% output.

risks_watch: Export recovery depends on Middle East normalisation and freight rates, currently $5,500-6,000 per container versus $400-500 before.
Chemical cost volatility and competitor discounting could force further price rollbacks or hikes; the Q1 margin gain may not persist.
Market share loss versus Century and rising capacity from Action (South India) and a new Madhya Pradesh line could keep pricing under pressure through FY27.
Channel destocking and hand-to-mouth buying may keep Q2 volumes below run-rate.
Forex loss of INR2.5 crore on the euro ECB, and plywood margin decline to 2.7% QoQ.
summary.management_tone: Cautious on near-term guidance, citing daily chemical and discount volatility, but confident on the structural case for margin recovery through volume and utilisation. Management was defensive when pressed on market share loss and on why it did not act as price leader.
key_quotes: Once the condition in the Middle East returns to normal, we can also expect the export flows to gradually improve as well.
But yes, I think the primary reason for that is overcapacity and you know, lack of enough orders for various customers, various companies, which is resulting in them reacting in this manner.
So, a double-digit margins are not, a very tough ask, to be honest with you.
At this point of time, because of the uncertainties, we would like to refrain from giving. We are not in control of what is happening with regards to the chemical costs.
Earlier we were priced at a premium to Century, we have now taken a decision that, we are going to be price competitive against all the peers in the market and price ourselves at par with them.

adds.what: Plywood capacity expansion of 30-40% via minimal debottlenecking investment in existing facility

growth.why: Management declined to give numeric revenue, margin or utilisation guidance, citing chemical cost and discount volatility; growth relies on ramping domestic volumes from ~51% utilisation with no MDF growth capex for 18-24 months, and exports and OEM are weak.
